the propensity to seek care in different healthcare systems is influenced by the organization of care and by the perceived communication between the patient and the GP.

the organization of primary care, patients’ perceived communication, and patients’ perceived accessibility of their primary care provider are associated with patients' propensity to seek healthcare for minor or severe symptoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question whether the organization of health care systems influences patients’ propensity to use health care services, but we found only limited evidence that patients’ propensity for health care use is associated with actual health care utilization.
the question how health care systems influence the use of health services.

the question whether patients’ propensity for health care seeking is associated with actual health care utilization and with avoidable hospitalization, but we found no evidence to suggest that patients with a high propensity to seek care have higher health care utilization or a lower risk of hospitalization for avoidable conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

patients’ decision to consult their GP is influenced by various factors and that these factors are not only related to patients’ individual preferences, but also to organizational factors of the primary care system.
a higher propensity to use GP services is not necessarily associated with more GP visits, nor with less avoidable hospitalization.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the organization of primary care is associated with patients’ health care seeking behavior, but this is only weakly related to patients’ actual health care utilization.

a high propensity to seek care may not always lead to more health care utilization, and that other factors such as the availability and organization of health care may be more important determinants of health care utilization than patients’ propensity to use health services.
the propensity to seek care can be a good indicator of health care utilization, but not necessarily for all aspects of health care use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between propensity to seek healthcare and actual healthcare use is not straightforward.
patients’ propensity is not a good indicator of the quality of care.

health care systems need to be aware of the influence that the organization of primary care has on patients’ care seeking behaviors, and to be aware that this may lead to overuse or even underuse of health care services.
